/** Canvas font string, e.g. canvasFont('title') → 'bold 32px "Trebuchet MS", …'. */
export function canvasFont(size: 'small' | 'body' | 'title', weight: 'normal' | 'bold' = 'normal') {
  return `${weight} ${theme.font[size]}px ${theme.font.family}`;
}

/** Exposes the theme to CSS as custom properties, e.g. --color-accent. */
export function applyTheme(root: HTMLElement = document.documentElement) {
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(theme.colors)) {
    root.style.setProperty(`--color-${name}`, value);
  }
  root.style.setProperty('--font-family', theme.font.family);
  root.style.setProperty('--radius', `${theme.radius}px`);
}

content.text:
The carnival now has a Halloween theme. `npm run check` passes (lint, formatting, types and all 63 tests), but I haven't looked at it in a browser yet. Run `npm run dev` and open localhost:5173 to see it.

**What changed** (on a new branch, `halloween-theme`, not committed yet):
- **Theme** (`src/carnival/theme.ts`): pumpkin-orange and purple stripes on a near-black purple background, bone-white text, candle-gold accent and blood-red for danger. Every game and the page's CSS read these colours, so all three games and the booth cards switch over without any changes of their own.
- **Midway map** (`src/midway/palette.ts`): a night sky fading from midnight to dusk purple, dark clouds, fog on the horizon, dead grass, dirt paths and dark hedges. The tents are orange and purple, and the bunting is orange, black, purple and gold. Balloons and shirts now come in Halloween colours too.
- **New scenery** (`src/midway/render.ts`, `src/midway/midway.ts`): a glowing full moon and four flapping bats that drift across the sky. They stay still if someone has reduced motion turned on.
- **Browser tab icon** (`index.html`): 🎪 is now 🎃.

**Things to know:**
- The water cannon is now a ghostly teal. The game also has one hard-coded blue (`#4fc3f7`, in `src/games/water-cannon/game.ts`) that skips the theme, so that bit stays blue. I left it alone because it's a separate house-rule problem.
- The repo's rules say changes to `src/carnival/` go in their own PR. This change touches the shared theme and the midway together, so you may want to split it when you open the PR.
- My first `npm run format` ran before dependencies were installed and reformatted some files I hadn't touched. I put those back, so the diff now only has the five files above.

Want me to commit this and open a PR?

# Add a carnival game

Every game is a booth in its own folder, built the same way as the water cannon.
Read `src/games/water-cannon/game.ts` first: it is the pattern to copy.

## Steps

1. **Pick the id.** Kebab-case, short and plain, such as `ring-toss`. The folder,
   the `id` and the URL (`#/play/ring-toss`) all use it.
2. **Create the folder** `src/games/<game-id>/` with three files:
   - `game.ts`
   - `game.test.ts`
   - `README.md`
3. **Write the logic as plain functions** in `game.ts`: a `createState()` and
   functions like `step(state, dt)` and the player's actions. Export them, and
   keep them free of the canvas and the DOM so Vitest can run them.
4. **Export the game** from `game.ts`, as a named export and as the default
   export. The default export is how the midway finds it:

   ```ts
   export const ringToss: CarnivalGame = {
     id: 'ring-toss',
     name: 'Ring Toss',
     description: 'One sentence for the midway.',
     start(canvas) {
       // size the canvas from theme.canvas, add listeners, start the loop
       return () => {
         // cancel the animation frame and remove the listeners
       };
     },
   };

   export default ringToss;
   ```

5. **Report the score once per round** with `recordScore(ringToss.id, score)`
   from `src/carnival`, when the round ends. Never use local storage directly.
6. **Draw with the theme.** Every colour is `theme.colors.*` and every font is
   `canvasFont(...)`. If the game needs a colour the theme lacks, use the closest
   theme colour and say so in the pull request. Adding a colour to
   `src/carnival/theme.ts` is its own change, never part of a game's.
7. **Don't touch `src/games/index.ts`.** It finds every folder whose `game.ts`
   has a default export, so the new game registers itself.
8. **Test the logic** in `game.test.ts`: the starting state, scoring, how a round
   ends, and any edge the README promises.
9. **Write the README:** how to play, how scoring works and the files in the folder.
10. **Run `npm run format`, then `npm run check`,** and fix anything it
    reports. If you can open a browser, also run `npm run dev`, walk to the new
    booth and play a round.

## Done when

- The game shows on the midway and is playable at `#/play/<game-id>`.
- Its best score shows on the midway after a round.
- `npm run check` passes, including the registry test that every game folder
  is registered.

input.content:
# Ghost Shooting Gallery

Ghosts float across three rows of the gallery, bobbing as they go. Zap as many
as you can before your shots run out.

## How to play

- Move the mouse to aim the crosshair, and click to zap the spot under it.
- You have 12 shots, and a miss uses one too. The round ends on your last shot.
- A zapped ghost vanishes in a poof and floats back in from the start of its row.
- Click again on the game over screen to play another round.

## Scoring

Each ghost scores 10 points for every 50 px/s of speed, rounded up:

| Row    | Speed    | Points |
| ------ | -------- | ------ |
| Top    | 200 px/s | 40     |
| Middle | 130 px/s | 30     |
| Bottom | 70 px/s  | 20     |

The best possible round is 12 top-row ghosts, for 480 points. Your final score
is saved to the carnival's score board when the round ends.

## Files

- `game.ts`: the game logic (`createState`, `zap`, `step`, `scoreForHit`,
  `isHit`, `ghostY`) and the `ghostShootingGallery` entry, the default export
  the midway finds.
- `game.test.ts`: tests for the game logic.

I built the Ghost Shooting Gallery and committed it locally on a new branch, `ghost-shooting-gallery`. I haven't played it in a browser yet, so the drawing and the feel are unchecked. Run `npm run dev` and walk to its booth, or go straight to `#/play/ghost-shooting-gallery`.

**How it plays:**
- Ghosts float across three rows, bobbing up and down, and their hems ripple as they move. They wrap around the edges.
- Move the mouse to aim a crosshair, and click to zap. You get 12 shots, and a miss uses one too.
- Faster ghosts score more: 40 points on the top row, 30 in the middle and 20 on the bottom, so the best round is 480. A zapped ghost disappears in a puff with "+points" above it, and comes back from the start of its row.
- The score is recorded once at the end of the round through the shared scores module. Every colour comes from the theme.
